$comment: Color tokens map 1:1 to --kavacha-* CSS custom properties on the chrome root.
$readBeforeEditing: EDITING THIS FILE DOES NOT CHANGE THE BROWSER. It is the reference copy of
the default theme, not its source. Midnight is the BAKED default: patch 0016
%includes its tokens into zen-theme.css at build time, and that build-time
floor is what paints before any JavaScript runs.
So this package has three consumers, none of which is the running default:
1. Documentation -- the reference implementation of the package format.
2. A starting point to copy into the profile's kavacha-themes/<id>/, where
it IS live and every token below takes effect.
3. Nothing else. The shipped default reads none of it.
To actually change the default look you must edit BOTH real sources:
src/zen/kavacha-theme/kavacha-midnight.inc.css   (the baked floor)
BUILTIN_THEMES['kavacha-midnight'] in KavachaThemeEngine.sys.mjs
and then mirror the change here. Recorded as defect D5 (resolved as
not-a-bug, kept as a maintenance trap); see documentation/REMAINING_WORK.md.
PATCH 0061 CHANGED THE VALUES BELOW, AND WHY THIS FILE MATTERS.
There used to be a FOURTH definition: kavacha-theme-fixes.inc.css (patch
0033) re-declared six of these tokens darker and, being %included last, was
the one on screen -- so this file, the floor and the engine all described a
theme nobody was looking at. 0033's values won the argument and are now the
values in all three places, including here.
The note that used to sit here saying the baked floor carries only
surface/text/border is also gone, because that was the bug: the engine used
to return early for the default theme, so the twelve tokens the floor did
not carry were undefined at the shipped default and their consumers fell
back to a currentColor mix. All eighteen are baked now and there is no early
return, so a token means the same thing whichever theme is active.
